reason: The cited evidence (E2) directly supports the existence of Cr/V segregation and its link to radiation-induced precipitation, but provides no data on annealing, homogenization, or the effect of removing segregation on precipitation and hardening, leaving the core intervention premises unsupported.
premises: As-deposited W38Ta36Cr15V11 exhibits Cr/V segregation at grain boundaries and triple junctions
This segregation seeds radiation-induced Cr/V-rich precipitates under irradiation to ~8 dpa
A rapid homogenization anneal can dissolve this segregation to achieve a uniform solid solution
Removing segregation prevents radiation-induced precipitation by eliminating nucleation sites
The homogenized alloy retains negligible irradiation hardening due to preserved defect sink characteristics
